subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests, and should that cache be limited to one shared reviewer instance keyed by the full reviewed input?
rationale: The bug is source-proven and narrow, but caching changes when a later exec bypasses a fresh model review in a safety-sensitive approval path, and sibling callers currently differ in reviewer lifetime.

options.title: Approve exact-input per-instance memo
options.body: Cache reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance using the full reviewed input as the key, without persisting or upgrading the approval.

options.title: Cover every helper caller
options.body: Also change helper callers that currently create a reviewer per request so repeated plugin or node-host helper reviews share the same cache lifetime.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated model completions to preserve one-request-one-review behavior until stronger security or billing evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-input per-instance memo
recommendation.body: Cache reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance using the full reviewed input as the key, without persisting or upgrading the approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame for the reviewer, both host call sites, and adjacent helper factories points to this recent area contributor.
